topic: The 'supremacy' of the gods over time

positions.name: Akkadian/Babylonian
positions.description: Enlil is the king of the gods

positions.name: Babylonian (later)
positions.description: Marduk is the king of the gods

how_we_present_it: We present the 'supremacy' as a political/theological development over time, not as a mythic event. We do NOT flatten the pantheon into one 'supreme god'.

positions.name: S4
positions.description: In some accounts they are 'sisters'; in others they are adversaries

how_we_present_it: We store both versions and note the variation.

positions.name: Atrahasis
positions.description: The flood-hero is Atrahasis; the flood is part of the creation-of-humanity story

positions.name: Gilgamesh
positions.description: The flood-hero is Utnapishtim; the flood is part of Gilgamesh's quest for immortality

how_we_present_it: We present both versions (Atrahasis and Gilgamesh) and note the differences.

positions.name: Akkadian (Ishtar) version
positions.description: The details vary (the 'stand-in' is sometimes not Dumuzi)

how_we_present_it: We present the Sumerian version as the primary and note the Akkadian variant.

positions.name: Sumerian
positions.description: The Sumerian texts are c. 3500-2000 BCE

positions.name: Babylonian
positions.description: The Babylonian texts (Enuma Elish, Gilgamesh) are c. 1800-1000 BCE

how_we_present_it: We make clear that the Sumerian religion is much older than the Babylonian texts that preserve it.

positions.name: Atrahasis
positions.description: From Apsu's flesh (the primeval fresh water)

how_we_present_it: We present both versions and note that they are distinct creation-accounts.
